quotes.text: PRAKASH NAYI @ SEN v. STATE OF GOA

The accused-appellant was convicted and sentenced u/s. 302 IPC for having caused the death of the victim-deceased by attacking him at a store in which the deceased was working, with an iron locking plate without any provocation and premeditation.

Penal Code, 1860 – ss. 302 and s.84 – Plea of Insanity – "Schizophrenia" – Accused-appellant was convicted and sentenced u/s. 302 IPC for having caused the death of the victim-deceased by attacking him at a store in which the deceased was working, with an iron locking plate without any provocation and premeditation.

Accused-appellant was convicted and sentenced u/s. 302 IPC for having caused the death of the victim-deceased by attacking him at a store in which the deceased was working, with an iron locking plate without any provocation and premeditation.

In the course of trial, the defence pleaded insanity – At one of the hospitals where the accused was undergoing the treatment before the date of incident, it was recorded that the accused was suffering from anxiety neurosis with reactive depression and has symptoms of acid peptic disease and mild hypertension and the treatment was akin to one meant for schizophrenia – Two doctors were examined before the Sessions Court wherein they deposed positively pointing towards schizophrenia.
On trial, the Trial Court convicted the accused of the said offence, and the Conviction was upheld by the High Court – Aggrieved by the decision, the accused approached Supreme Court

Allowing the appeal, the Court HELD : 1. Section 84 of the IPC recognizes only an act which could not be termed as an offence. It starts with the words "nothing is an offence". The said words are a clear indication of the intendment behind this laudable provision. Such an act shall emanate from an unsound mind. Therefore, the existence of an unsound mind is a sine qua non to the applicability of the provision.

neutral_facts.value: The accused attacked the deceased at a store where the deceased was working, using an iron locking plate without any provocation or premeditation. The incident occurred on 14.05.2004 at 6:00 a.m. The accused was treated at a hospital prior to the incident for anxiety neurosis with reactive depression, acid peptic disease, and mild hypertension, with treatment akin to that for schizophrenia. The accused was examined by two doctors who opined he suffered from schizophrenia. The trial court convicted the accused, but the Supreme Court overturned the conviction, finding the courts below erred in not accepting the medical reports and in not considering the accused's prior insanity. The accused was found to be unfit to stand trial at the time of the incident, and his subsequent fitness to face trial was deemed indicative of his prior insanity.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that Section 84 of the IPC recognizes only acts done by a person who, at the time of the act, was incapable of knowing the nature of the act or that it was wrong or contrary to law. The court emphasized the need for legal insanity, not mere medical insanity.
